item.title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.14807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Juan Jos\'e Mar\'in

item.title: Isomorphic embeddings of $L_q(0,1)$ into Lorentz--Schatten ideals
item.dc:creator: Chenhao Gao, Jinghao Huang

item.title: Optimal approximation results for non-standard growth functionals in the super-dimensional case
item.description: arXiv:2611.15428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the super-dimensional case $p>n$ we show that $W^{1,p}$-functions can be uniformly approximated by H\"older continuous functions with improved exponent $\frac {p-n}{p-1}$. We use this to show density of smooth functions and absence of Lavrentiev's phenomenon for $(p, q)$-growth with optimal conditions. The special cases of double phase and Musielak--Orlicz growth are also included. Finally, we improve the conditions for maximal regularity of the double phase minimizers. In each case the optimality of our range of exponents is shown by known examples.
item.dc:creator: Peter H\"ast\"o, Jihoon Ok

item.title: Semigroups with periodic complex-time boundedness and holomorphy regions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the periodicity of complex-time boundedness and holomorphy domains of operator semigroups. We show that an imaginary-time covariance identity involving an isometry yields periodicity of these domains. The method is applied to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator and the hypoelliptic Laplacian on the circle, providing a spectral explanation of periodicity independent of the explicit geometry of their boundedness regions. We also discuss the distinction between boundedness and contractivity, using the classical heat semigroup as an example.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: Hypercyclic Algebras for Weighted Double Shifts
item.description: arXiv:2611.15559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on the approach of Bayart, Costa J\'unior and Papathanasiou, we establish a Baire criterion for possibly noncommuting operator pairs to support hypercyclic algebras, with hypercyclicity defined through all finite compositions.We then study weighted double backward shifts under different multiplications and topologies.We characterize the existence of hypercyclic algebras for coordinatewise multiplication on sequence algebras admitting a continuous norm and, separately, on $\omega^2=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N_0^2}$ with the product topology.For the noncommutative triangular product induced by upper triangular matrix multiplication, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of dense hypercyclic algebras on $\omega^2$.In this setting, their existence is equivalent to that of one freely generated by countably infinitely many elements.Finally, we exhibit a pair on a fixed Fr\'echet space that supports a dense hypercyclic algebra for coordinatewise multiplication and a nonzero hypercyclic algebra, but no dense one, for the triangular product.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Chen, Wei Wang, Ze-hua Zhou

item.title: Sampled resolvents of $C_0$-semigroups: aliasing and sharp rates on the Crandall-Pazy scale
item.description: arXiv:2611.15563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a $C_0$-semigroup $(S_t)$ with generator $B$, sampling the Laplace integral $(\lambda-B)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}S_t\,dt$ on the grid $T\mathbb{N}$ gives $Q_T=T(I-e^{-\lambda T}S_T)^{-1}$, the impulse-invariant discretization of the resolvent. The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $\lambda-2\pi in/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. Our main result is a sharp scale of rates for the trapezoid correction $Q_T-\frac T2I$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $\alpha\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/\alpha})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^\alpha)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{\alpha+\theta})$ on the interpolation space of order $\theta$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+\alpha})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $\alpha$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda$. This interpolates between unitary groups with unbounded generator ($\alpha=0$, no convergence in norm) and analytic semigroups ($\alpha=1$), and every exponent is attained. For smooth data an Euler--Maclaurin expansion justifies Romberg extrapolation. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations. Experiments, including a structurally damped string whose semigroup is of Gevrey class, confirm the rates.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Castillo

item.title: Strongly reducible operators in factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.15586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a factor acting on a separable complex Hilbert space. For every operator $T$ in $\mathcal M$ with dense generalized kernel and $T^2\ne 0$, we characterize the strong reducibility of $T$ relative to $\mathcal M$ based on a $3\times 3$ asymmetric matrix representation of $T$. As applications, we obtain criteria for the strong reducibility of algebraic operators in finite factors and type $\mathrm{III}$ factors. We also prove that every Hilbert space operator with an infinite-dimensional multicyclic direct summand is similar to an irreducible operator.
item.dc:creator: Minghui Ma, Rui Shi, Jianming Yang, Shanshan Yang

item.title: Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.15604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Shiqi Liu, Hongyin Zhao

item.title: Path Components of Almost Doubly Commuting Fredholm Tuples
item.description: arXiv:2611.15994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we prove that the Fredholm index classifies the norm-path components of almost doubly commuting Fredholm n-tuples on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space. Using Kasparov's technical theorem, we join each tuple to an essentially normal one by a straight-line Fredholm path and applying the Douglas-Curto theorem.
item.dc:creator: Chen Li, Guohao Li, Kai Wang

item.title: Convolution on quantum tori I: Sharp Young inequalities and endpoint Sobolev embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a convolution of noncommutative tori. The construction is the preadjoint of a trace-preserving cocycle-addition homomorphism. Its zero-parameter case is the function--operator semi-convolution. We prove both mixed $L_{1}$--$L_\infty$ inequalities and various Young inequalities with the optimal constant one, including their limiting cases. The endpoint bounds also yield submajorization and convolution estimates in fully symmetric spaces. As applications, we establish, for every integer $k\geq1$ and $1\leq p\leq\infty$, $W_{p}^{k}(\mathbb{T}_{\theta}^{d})\hookrightarrow B_{\infty,\infty}^{k-\frac{d}{p}}(\mathbb{T}_{\theta}^{d})$, and prove the critical embedding $W_{1}^{d}(\mathbb{T}_{\theta}^{d})\hookrightarrow L_\infty(\mathbb{T}_{\theta}^{d})$. These results settle the two questions posed in Remark~6.8 of Xiong, Xu and Yin \cite{XiongXuYin}.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Sukochev, Ramazan Tastankul, Kanat Tulenov, Dmitriy Zanin

item.title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.16448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a transform-adapted approximation framework for shallow neural networks based on the short-time special affine Fourier transform (STSAFT). Replacing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the definition of classical modulation spaces, we work with weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces, building on the existing SAFT-associated modulation-space framework, and use their chirp correspondence with classical weighted modulation spaces through the chirp factorization of the SAFT kernel. We construct an associated neural dictionary and establish an $N$-term Sobolev approximation bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ on bounded one-dimensional domains. A global approximation theorem is also obtained when the spatial translation parameter ranges over the whole real line; a compact-support argument explains why an unrestricted global conclusion cannot in general be inferred from a bounded translation range. For a fixed-scale chirp family $f_\kappa(x)=e^{i\pi\kappa x^2}u(x)$, we combine the global estimate with a phase analysis to obtain the stronger phase-dependent upper-bound factor $\langle\lambda\rangle^n\langle\kappa-\lambda\rangle^{n+3/2-1/r}.$ For each fixed nonzero Schwartz envelope, matching the dictionary phase reduces the growth of this specified upper bound from order $|\kappa|^{n+3/2-1/r}$ to order $|\kappa|^n$, while preserving the $N^{-1/2}$ rate. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. We discuss the effective number of fitted output coefficients, including the rank loss of the sine branch at zero phase, and distinguish the numerical diagnostics from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.
item.dc:creator: Ming Hu, Bei Liu, Bolin Liu, Jie Shen

item.title: Analogs of crystalline measures in tube sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.16506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a pure point complex measure on a tube set $R^d+i F$, where $F$ is a compact convex subset in $R^d$, such that this tube set is the minimal closed convex tube set containing support of $\mu$. Furthermore, assume that the Fourier transform $\hat\mu$ (in the sense of distributions) is a measure. We determine conditions on the measure $\mu$ under which the variation of the measure $\hat\mu$ grows at least as $\exp\{2\pi H_F(t)\}$, as well as conditions under which this variation grows at most as $\exp\{2\pi H_F(t)\}$; here $H_F(t)$ is the support function of $F$.
item.dc:creator: \"{O}zkan De\v{g}er, Sergii Favorov

item.title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fr\'echet differentiability
item.description: arXiv:2611.16777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fr\'echet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Ti\v{s}er. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fr\'echet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzhe Wang

item.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
item.description: arXiv:2611.16997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.
item.dc:creator: Bonan Chen, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo

item.title: Augmented Dynamical Sampling under unmodeled Forcing
item.description: arXiv:2611.17137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study recovery of an initial state from dynamical samples of a trajectory driven by unknown additive forcing. Measurements against both the original sensors and their images under the adjoint nominal evolution yield one-step residuals that cancel the initial state exactly. These residuals separate forcing estimation from initial-state reconstruction. For a centered Gaussian forcing model with fixed covariance parameters, we combine Gaussian conditioning with canonical dual-frame reconstruction and derive an exact unconditional second-moment identity, including the correlation between the forcing-estimation error and the measurement noise. We also obtain high-probability bounds and identify the irreducible forcing uncertainty through a conditional covariance in the geometry induced by the prior. A hierarchy of augmented sensor systems separates the role of sampling depth in forcing visibility from that of the observation horizon in nominal observability. An image-transport experiment and finite-dimensional and periodic-convolution experiments illustrate the residual correction and the separate roles of sampling depth and observation horizon.
item.dc:creator: Juan Giribet, Serena Feldberg

item.title: Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
item.description: arXiv:2611.17140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by \[ \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}: \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}} \left| \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}} {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2} \right|<1 \right\}, \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0 \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $\mu_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,\mu_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $\Psi_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[ \Psi_{\mathbb H}(\xi_1, \xi_2,\lambda_1,\lambda_2) = \left(\frac{\lambda_1(\xi_1-1)}{2}, \frac{\xi_2(\xi_1+1)}{2}, \ \frac{\lambda_1\lambda_2(\xi_1+1)}{2}, \ \xi_1 \xi_2\lambda_1\lambda_2 \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $\Psi_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Pal, Guicong Su, Nitin Tomar

item.title: Frames and representing systems in Hardy spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study representing systems of Cauchy kernels or dilations of a given function in Hardy spaces. We give a complete geometric description of countable sets $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{D}$ such that the system $\{\hat{k}_{\lambda}\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of normalized Cauchy kernels forms a generalized frame in the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{D})$ with $p \in (1, \infty)$ with respect to a particular coefficient space. For a wide class of functions we construct representing systems of their dilations in $H^2$. We also obtain a linear method for expanding functions in series of Cauchy kernels in $H^2$.
item.dc:creator: Timur Batenev

item.title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$. Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous. We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(\Omega)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Kr\'ol, Yuri Latushkin, Yuri Tomilov

item.title: On the Equivalence of Linear and $C^*$ Extremality for Unital Completely Positive Maps on Commutative Real $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.15383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital commutative real $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal H$ be a finite dimensional real Hilbert space. In this article, an easily verifiable necessary and sufficient condition for a linear extreme unital completely positive (UCP) map $\Phi:\mathcal A \rightarrow B(\mathcal H)$ to be C*-extreme, is obtained. As an application, the $C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A$ on which linear extreme UCP maps coincide with the $C^*$-extreme ones, are classified.
item.dc:creator: Sriram Balasubramanian, Karthikeyan Thangaraj

item.title: A Rigorous Fredholm Framework and Stabilized Equal-Order Finite Element Methods for the Time-Harmonic Biot Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.15495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and finite element approximation of a three-field formulation of the time-harmonic Biot model, motivated by frequency-domain magnetic resonance elastography. The underlying complex-valued mixed variational problem is noncoercive because of the inertial elasticity term and the coupled three-field structure. Continuous well-posedness is established under a non-resonance condition by decomposing the variational operator into an invertible principal part and a compact perturbation and applying the Fredholm alternative. We then develop stabilized equal-order finite element methods based on momentum-residual stabilization and local projection stabilization of the pore pressure. For the discrete problem, we establish mesh-uniform stability and well-posedness on sufficiently fine meshes via an a priori stability estimate and a Schatz-type compactness argument, without invoking discrete $T$-coercivity. Optimal-order a priori error estimates are derived in the natural energy norm. We also develop systematic selection principles for the stabilization parameters. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate stable approximations for heterogeneous low-permeability media and anatomically realistic brain geometries relevant to magnetic resonance elastography.
item.dc:creator: Mingchao Cai, Yiming Fu, Jingzhi Li

item.title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.15672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.
item.dc:creator: Ram\'on Aliaga, Rub\'en Medina

item.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.15930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how stability and the independence property of the norm formula $\varphi(x,y)=\lVert x+y\rVert$ on a real Banach space relate to the same properties in its complete theory. We construct separable Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ and a separable elementary extension $W$ of $X$. The norm formula is stable on $X$ and has the independence property on $W$, and therefore in $\operatorname{Th}(X)$. It is unstable on $Y$ and has no independence property in any model of $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$. Together with $\ell_2$ and $X\oplus_2Y$, these spaces realize all five possible combinations of stability, instability without the independence property, and the independence property on a space with the presence or absence of the independence property in its complete theory. All five spaces are uniformly convex and $\sqrt3$-isomorphic to Hilbert space. Their norms satisfy the common midpoint estimate $\lVert x\rVert,\lVert y\rVert\leq1 \Longrightarrow \lVert(x+y)/2\rVert^2\leq1-(1/12)\lVert x-y\rVert^2$, and $W$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. The proof for $Y$ uses coordinate truncation and a polynomial bound on threshold patterns for vectors of bounded support. These bounds give finite fat-shattering dimension at each positive scale, from which the complete-theory conclusion follows.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Poitevin

item.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.16007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(\sigma)$ to $L^q(\omega)$ for the operator $H_\sigma g(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,d\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $\omega$ is a $\sigma$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $\kappa_{p,q}$ in $C_*\le\kappa_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $\omega$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Os\k{e}kowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Kanjilal

item.title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.16043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for It\^o diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem. More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehat\mu_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\delta_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehat\mu_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$. In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehat\mu_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2\lambda_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2\lambda_d}$, where $\lambda_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.
item.dc:creator: Simon Coste

item.title: Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.16734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $\Omega$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partial\Omega$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $\Omega = U$.
item.dc:creator: Erik Avelin

item.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang

item.title: Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
item.description: arXiv:2611.17071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.
item.dc:creator: Jaouad Mourtada

item.title: Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embeddings: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2406.08091v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the necessary and sufficient conditions on domain for Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embedding of the space $W^{1,\Phi(\cdot,\cdot)}(\Omega)$ where $\Phi(x,t):=t^{p(x)}{(\log(e+t))}^{q(x)}.$
item.dc:creator: Ankur Pandey, Nijjwal Karak

item.title: Maximal non-compactness of embeddings between sequence spaces
item.description: arXiv:2510.24290v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We will focus on studying the ball measure of non-compactness $\alpha(T)$ for various particular instances of embedding operators in sequence spaces. Our first main goal is to find necessary and sufficient conditions for an identity operator to be maximally non-compact. Next, we will focus on studying Lorentz sequence spaces $\ell^{p,q}$ and their basic properties. We will characterize the inclusions between Lorentz sequence spaces depending on the values of $p$ and $q$. Then we will try to determine exact values of the norms of the identity operators between these embedded spaces. Lastly, we will determine whether these identity operators are maximally non-compact by using our general theorems.
item.dc:creator: Anna Kneselov\'a

item.title: Logarithmic double phase embeddings with variable exponents: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2511.13286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the necessary and sufficient conditions in the domain for Sobolev-type embedding of the space $W^{1,\Phi(\cdot,\cdot)}(\Omega)$ where $\Phi(x,t):=t^{p(x)}+ a(x) t^{q(x)}\log^{r(x)}(e+t)$ with $1\leq p(x)\leq q(x).$ We have established subcritical embedding in bounded John domains under some regularity assumptions on exponents $p,$ $q,$ $r$, and $a$. Conversely, we have proved that if the embedding holds in any domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^n,$ then $\Omega$ must satisfy the log-measure density condition.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Pandey, Nijjwal Karak

item.title: Frame constructions associated with operator orbits
item.description: arXiv:2605.29671v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies frames in Hilbert spaces generated by the orbits of finitely many vectors under a single operator, presenting new results on normal operators and multiplication operators as well as on operators composed of Jordan blocks. These results generalize existing results of Cabrelli, Molter, Paternostro and Philipp by means of techniques which deal with weighted interpolation, weighted composition operators, and Beurling--Lax theory related to shifts of finite multiplicity. Likewise, we discuss Carleson frames and construct counterexamples to a recent conjecture of Aldroubi, Cabrelli, Krishtal and Molter, showing that the relevant necessary condition is of density type rather than the M\"untz--Sz\'asz condition. Moreover, by using the theory of weighted composition operators, we answer a question of Cheshmavar on frames produced by iterative multiplication. Finally, for orbits of infinitely many vectors the underlying model is a shift of infinite multiplicity which, by a theorem of Rota, is a universal operator; consequently, a complete description of such frames along these lines would encompass the Invariant Subspace Problem.
item.dc:creator: Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez, Jonathan R. Partington

item.title: The Bishop--Phelps--Bollob\'as Property for Extremally Disconnected Ranges
item.description: arXiv:2606.12080v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb F$ be either $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $L$ be a nonempty extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space. We show that $(X,C(L,\mathbb F))$ has the Bishop--Phelps--Bollob\'as property with $\eta(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2/2$ for every Banach space $X$ over $\mathbb F$. For each fixed $L$ and either scalar field, this bound is optimal uniformly over $X$.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Priyadarshi Dey, Chunlin Liu, Monika

item.title: Translation Continuity and the Structure of Infinite-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.24718v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For Baker's Borel-rectangle measure $\mu$ and $1\le p<\infty$, we classify the continuous vectors of each one-parameter translation group on $L^p(\mu)$. For each $v\in\mathbb{R}^\mathbb{N}$, the continuous vectors form a projection band, which coincides with the whole space when $v$ has finite support, is trivial when $v\notin\ell^1$, and is nonzero and proper otherwise. We also establish in ZFC the isometric classification considered in [Isometric classification of the $L^{p}$-spaces of infinite dimensional Lebesgue measure, Banach J. Math. Anal. 20 (2026), no. 1, Paper No. 7], showing that both $L^p(\mu)$ and the kernel of restriction to integer cubes are lattice isometric to $\ell^p(\mathfrak{c},L^p[0,1])$. When $v\in\ell^1\setminus c_{00}$, the continuous band and its disjoint complement have the same lattice-isometric structure, with the latter contained in the cube-restriction kernel.
item.dc:creator: Daniel L. Rodr\'iguez-Vidanes, Juan Carlos Sampedro

item.title: Invariance Preserving Conjugation and Linear Operators on the Hardy Space
item.description: arXiv:2607.13915v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study linear and anti-linear operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ in connection with the Beurling lattice. First, in contrast to Sarason's result \cite{S1}, we show that no non-zero anti-linear operator leaves every shift-invariant subspace invariant. Then we completely characterize the class of conjugations, isometries, and invertible linear operators preserving the shift-invariant subspace structure in terms of weighted composition operators induced by disk automorphisms--combined with the canonical conjugation, isometric multiplication, and invertible Toeplitz operators, respectively. We also establish the existence and non-existence of conjugations that map shift-invariant subspaces to coinvariant subspaces. Finally, we construct a counterexample that rules out an analogous factorization for bounded linear operators preserving shift-invariance of closed images.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Supratim Jana

item.title: The linear scale in metric cotype for Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.08754v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We answer a question of Eskenazis, Mendel, and Naor by proving that the optimal universal scaling parameter in metric cotype $2$ for complete Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature has order $n$. The upper bound follows from a dyadic application of the Lang--Schroeder inequality, and the lower bound follows from snowflake universality of $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$.
item.dc:creator: Longfa Sun, Yipeng Zhang

item.title: The Strong Naor--Schechtman Convolution Inequality on the Product of Cyclic Groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.15768v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we resolve the convolution inequality problem posed by Naor and Schechtman in \cite[Question 6.1]{N-S2016} (see also \cite{Na2016}). More precisely, we establish the following strong convolution inequality on products of finite cyclic groups: For each $1\leq p<\infty$ there exists $c_{p}>0$ such that for every $n$, $m\in \mathbb{N}$ the following holds \[ \begin{split} &\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x+\varepsilon)-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x-\varepsilon)\right|^{p}\\ \leq& c^{p}_{p}\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|\varepsilon_{j}\left[E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x+e_{j})-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x-e_{j})\right]\right|^{p}, \end{split} \] $E_{A}f(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{\delta\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}f\left(x+\sum_{j\in A}\delta_{j}e_{j}\right)$ for every $A\subseteq \{1,\cdots,n\}$. The growth order we obtain here $c_{p}=O(p)$ as $p\to \infty$. For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.
item.dc:creator: Yong Jiao, Sijie Luo, Dmitriy Zanin, Dejian Zhou

item.title: Crossed-Heinz Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.04567v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For positive matrices $A,B$ and $p,q>0$, the second author (2009) asked whether the inequality \[ \|A^pB^q+B^pA^q\|\leq \|A^{p+q}+B^{p+q}\| \] holds for every unitarily invariant norm. Despite a series of papers addressing this question, as well as recent intensive computational and AI-assisted investigations by Matthew Colbrook (2026, \cite{Col}), the problem remains open. It is a striking example of how an elementary scalar statement can become extremely difficult to handle in the noncommutative setting. Some partial positive results are known. In this note, we provide one more: the crossed-Heinz inequality holds for two-by-two matrices. This result also leads to a new and elegant characterization of the singular values of two-by-two matrices. In arbitrary dimension, we turn to the special case $p=q=1$, obtaining a series of eigenvalue estimates for the anticommutator $AB+BA$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Sababheh, Jean-Christophe Bourin

item.title: Structured coordinate systems in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. For every $1 \leq p< \infty$, we obtain bases of non-negative functions with basis constants arbitrarily close to one, as well as bases with positive biorthogonal functionals. For every $2 \leq p < \infty$, we construct Schauder bases consisting of translates of a single function, which can be chosen to extend to an entire function. When $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$. Finally, for $p>2$, the entire function generating the basis of translates can also be chosen non-negative.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Freeman, Lukas Liehr, Mitchell A. Taylor

item.title: Characters on star algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.33579v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study conditions under which a unital linear functional on a complex star algebra is multiplicative. We introduce a class of star algebras, called AC*-algebras, which captures certain algebraic properties of unital C*-algebras. Our main result characterizes positive characters on unital AC*-algebras through a nonvanishing condition on a distinguished subset of the algebra. This provides an algebraic counterpart to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem and addresses questions concerning the characterization of characters by nonvanishing conditions. We apply the result to unital C*-algebras and self-adjoint function algebras whose real parts are sublattices. We further obtain a Banach-Stone-type theorem for realcompact spaces, characterizing homeomorphisms in terms of bijective invertibility-preserving linear maps between their algebras of continuous complex-valued functions.
item.dc:creator: Karim Boulabiar

item.title: The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.39769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: Flows on uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2411.06999v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a uniformly locally finite metric space $(X, d)$, we investigate \emph{coarse} flows on its uniform Roe algebra $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, defined as one-parameter groups of automorphisms whose differentiable elements include all partial isometries arising from partial translations on $X$. We first show that any flow $\sigma$ on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ corresponds to a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ such that $\sigma_t(a) = e^{ith} a e^{-ith}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, allowing us to focus on operators $h$ that generate flows on $ \mathrm{C}^*_u (X)$. Assuming Yu's property A, we prove that a self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ induces a coarse flow on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ if and only if $h$ can be expressed as $h = a + d$, where $a \in \mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ and $d$ is a diagonal operator with entries forming a coarse function on $X$. We further study cocycle equivalence and cocycle perturbations of coarse flows, showing that, under property A, any coarse flow is a cocycle perturbation of a diagonal flow. Finally, for self-adjoint operators $h$ and $k$ that induce coarse flows on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, we characterize conditions under which the associated flows are either cocycle perturbations of each other or cocycle conjugate. In particular, if $h - k$ is bounded, then the flow induced by $h$ is a cocycle perturbation of the flow induced by $k$.
item.dc:creator: Bruno de Mendon\c{c}a Braga, Alcides Buss, Ruy Exel

item.title: Analysis of non-linear fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets
item.description: arXiv:2505.10455v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article addresses three problems: (1) the construction of a general nonlinear fractal interpolation function on post-critically finite (PCF) self-similar sets; (2) the study of the energy and normal derivatives of uniform nonlinear fractal functions; and (3) the estimation of the box-counting dimensions of the proposed fractal functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket and the von Koch curve. We present a general framework for constructing attractors and fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets using Edelstein contractions. Further, we derive upper and lower bounds for the box-counting dimensions of the graphs of nonlinear interpolants. Finally, we provide several graphical and numerical examples to illustrate the construction and estimate the dimensions for different data sets.
item.dc:creator: Aaryan Dharmesh Shah, Sangita Jha, Anarul Islam Mondal

item.title: Banach-Valued Carr\'e du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2512.08919v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a projective-tensor-valued carr\'e du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fr\'echet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carr\'e du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Solesne Bourguin, Simon Campese

item.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
item.description: arXiv:2604.18540v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.
item.dc:creator: Leon Bungert, Lucas Schmitt

item.title: Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
item.description: arXiv:2605.14699v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragi\v{c}evi\'c for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schr\"odinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Luciano Morelato, Andrea Poggio

item.title: Improvement of a Hardy-Littlewood inequality and applications to the boundedness of analytic paraproducts on mixed norm spaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.28080v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ denote the space of analytic functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For $0<p<\infty$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, let $M_p^p(r,f)=\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^p \frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$ and $M_\infty(r,f) = \sup_{|z|=r}|f(z)|$. For $0<p<q\leq \infty$, Hardy and Littlewood proved the prevalent inequality $$M_q(r,f)\le C(p,q)\frac{M_p(\rho,f)}{(\rho-r)^{\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}}}$$ for $0\leq r<\rho\leq 1$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$. In this paper, we obtain an improvement of this well-known inequality which is employed to characterize the symbols $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ such that the analytic paraproducts $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(\zeta)g'(\zeta)\,d\zeta$, $S_gf(z)=\int_0^z f'(\zeta)g(\zeta)\,d\zeta$ and $M_gf(z)=f(z)g(z)$, are bounded between two different mixed-norm spaces $A^{p,q}_\omega=\{ g\in \mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}): \int_0^1 M_p^q(r,g) \omega(r)\,dr<\infty\}$ induced by a radial doubling weight $\omega$. En route to the proof of these characterizations, we consider an open Carleson measure problem posed by Luecking and we solve it in a meaningful particular case.
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Miguel Moreno, Jos\'e \'Angel Pel\'aez

item.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2606.02786v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper is concerned with $\alpha$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $\alpha$-stable SDE.
item.dc:creator: Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue

item.title: Fast approximation and learning of binary classification tasks in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2607.01266v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study binary classification tasks whose decision sets are given by definable sets in o-minimal expansions of the real field. Motivated by the cell decomposition theory of definable sets, we introduce traceable sets that isolate the analytical properties of definable sets used for fast approximation by ReLU neural networks. Under uniform bounds on the number of cells and a suitable extension assumption for the boundary functions, we prove that classifiers can be approximated in $L^p$ up to accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ by ReLU neural networks of size $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-p(n-1)/m})$, with depth independent of $\varepsilon$ and polynomially bounded weights. This establishes quantitative approximation rates for suitable definable collections in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks. Furthermore, the stated approximation rates are also derived for definable maps under similar geometric assumptions on their smoothness domains. We then obtain statistical learning rates for empirical risk minimization with hinge loss over the approximating ReLU neural network classes. For $N$ uniformly distributed samples, the predicted classifiers achieve expected misclassification error of order $N^{-m/(m+n-1)}$ up to an arbitrarily small polynomial loss.
item.dc:creator: Clemens Kinn, Philipp Petersen

item.title: Isometric embeddings of trees: why 32 leaves can require six dimensions, and bounds for every tree
item.description: arXiv:2608.16288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify the first failure of the $\lceil\log_2 t\rceil$ leaf-count bound for isometric embeddings of $t$-leaf trees under the maximum norm. Every tree with at most $31$ leaves attains the bound, but a $32$-leaf tree requires six dimensions. This answers a question of Fitzpatrick and Nowakowski and disproves a conjecture of Aksoy, K{\i}l{\i}\c{c} and Ko\c{c}ak. We explain this failure by showing how requirements within and between branches force an additional coordinate. For a family of three-branch trees, we prove that the leaf bound is attained exactly when the two larger branches have equal leaf counts; otherwise, one additional coordinate is necessary. We also prove that every tree embeds in $\lceil 1.162832\log_2 t\rceil$ dimensions, improving the coefficient of approximately $1.44042$ established in 2005. These results hold for arbitrary positive edge lengths and the entire metric realization. We also construct infinite families in which the excess persists under repeated leaf expansion. Both main theorems are formalised in Lean using only standard axioms.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers

item.title: Noncommutative Maximal Ergodic Theorems for Modulated $(C,\alpha)$-Averages with Operator-Valued Weights
item.description: arXiv:2609.23616v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study modulated $(C,\alpha)$-ergodic averages with operator-valued weights and their subsequential versions in the setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras. Our framework combines $(C,\alpha)$-type modulation with operator-valued weights and extends both scalar-weighted and operator-valued weighted ergodic theories. We establish mean ergodic theorems and maximal inequalities for these averages on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We then study bilateral almost uniform and almost uniform convergence in noncommutative Orlicz spaces, including convergence along subsequences of density one when $\alpha\geq 1$. A key ingredient in our approach is the introduction of the $p$-convexity condition on the underlying Orlicz function. This condition allows us to transfer appropriate maximal estimates from noncommutative $L_p$-spaces to establish bilateral uniform equicontinuity in measure at zero on the corresponding noncommutative $p$-convex Orlicz spaces. Together with the noncommutative Banach principle, this yields the desired pointwise convergence results. As an additional consequence of our $p$-convexity argument, we extend Rota theorem to a larger class of noncommutative Orlicz spaces associated with the $p$-convex Orlicz functions considered in this article.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Debabrata De, Disha Shaw

item.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
item.description: arXiv:2611.08901v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations. We extend the theorem to every separable metric space, and in particular to every Polish space, by admitting countable suprema and infima according to weights computed from the construction. For a countable, uniformly bounded separating family whose supremum metric makes the space separable, the functions so built are exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and their uniform limits are exactly the bounded uniformly continuous functions. The theorem was discovered, and first proved, in infinitary real-valued logic, where the weights are the a priori bounds of formulas and the uniform approximation is equivalent to an approximate form of Beth's definability theorem, which carries Reggio's correspondence from compact spaces to separable metric spaces. The same bounds draw an exact line between the two forms of definability when the values of the coordinates in the models of the implicit definition form a set separable for the supremum metric: an implicitly defined predicate has an explicit definition precisely when the defining function is Lipschitz, and admits uniform approximation by sentences precisely when that function is uniformly continuous. We also give a purely topological-analytic proof of the theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: An almost sharp $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$-$L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.12463v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}} f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} whenever \begin{equation*} \mathcal{U}:= \min{\left\{ \min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}>1, \end{equation*} and we necessarily have $\mathcal{U}\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Abdelhakim
